_doc: docs/2026-10-13-congo-species-sources.md (numbers in brackets are its source list)

african_leopard.body.massBySexKg: [1],[2]: male 31-65, female 17-58; forest animals lower in the range (assumption: F 30, M 45)
african_leopard.locomotion.walkMs/trotMs: assumption: typical for a 30-45 kg cat
african_leopard.locomotion.sprintStaminaS: assumption: forest attacks are short ambush lunges; full sprints under ~20 s
african_leopard.locomotion.terrainCost/floodedTerrainCos: assumption: wades and swims short distances; never chases into water [1],[7]
african_leopard.senses: assumption: dense understorey limits sight to 20-40 m
african_leopard.diet.dailyIntakeKg: [8]: 1.6-4.9 kg/day; 2.5 kg chosen (assumption) with the Phase 1 density so two small prey species can sustain the leopards
african_leopard.hunting.preferredPrey: [4],[6]: duikers and chevrotains are taken; Phase 1 has only these two prey
african_leopard.hunting.maxPreyKg/preferredPreyKg: [1],[4]: prefers 10-40 kg; mean forest prey 19.7-31.6 kg; Phase 1 prey are 4-12 kg
african_leopard.hunting.baseSuccess: assumption: sim-tuned contest parameter, as the island leopard's; forest attack success 15-25% [9]
african_leopard.hunting.cachesKills: [2],[10]: no forest study reports caching; no kleptoparasites in rainforest
african_leopard.social.territory: [4]: Taï male 86 km², females 22-29 km² (assumption: Gabon F 25, M 80)
african_leopard.lifecycle: [1]: gestation 96 d, litter 2-3, weaned ~90 d, mature ~771-937 d, max 17 y, 15-24 months between litters
african_leopard.hunting.preferredPrey/preyPreference (2A: [3],[4],[23]: Lopé diet: ungulates 59% of biomass, red river hog 20%, buffalo 13% (calves and young), mean prey 29.2 kg; 10-40 kg preferred; weights are assumptions from these shares; golden cat taken rarely (intraguild) [6]
african_leopard.diet/offRosterShare: [23] Henschel et al. 2005 (Lopé, 196 scats): by biomass 59% ungulates, 18% diurnal primates, 17% large rodents (cane rat 13%); 0.35 = primates + large rodents, prey the world does not hold

blue_duiker.locomotion: assumption: small antelope: walk 0.6-0.9, trot 2-3, zig-zag dash 8-10 m/s for 2-5 s
blue_duiker.senses/escape: assumption: sight 15-25 m, FID 10-20 m; freezes first [12],[13]
blue_duiker.diet: [11],[12],[13]: ~3/4 fruit (modelled as fallen fruit and seed, 'roots') and browse; water mostly from food (assumption)
blue_duiker.diet.dailyIntakeKg: assumption: ~0.15 kg dry matter ≈ 0.45 kg fresh
blue_duiker.lifecycle: [12],[14]: gestation 196-216 d, 1 young, weaned 70-90 d, mature 270-540 d, max 12 y, ~265 d between births

water_chevrotain.locomotion: assumption: short legs: walk 0.4-0.7, dash 5-7 m/s for 2-4 s to water
water_chevrotain.locomotion.swims: [19],[20]: dives and swims underwater, up to ~4 min; swim speed assumption 0.7 m/s
water_chevrotain.senses/escape: assumption: nocturnal: sight 10-20 m; freezes first, then to water [19]
water_chevrotain.diet.dailyIntakeKg: assumption: ~0.3 kg dry matter ≈ 0.9 kg fresh
water_chevrotain.social: [19]: solitary, not territorial; female 13-14 ha, male 20-30 ha
water_chevrotain.lifecycle: [18],[19]: gestation 188-272 d, 1 young, weaned 90-180 d, mature 270-790 d, max 13-14 y, ~12 months between births

_population: CONGO_POPULATION (packages/sim/src/forest.ts), over 2,304 km2: blue duiker 18,000 (field 16/km2 in its habitat [15], lowered for the budget now that red duikers share the floor); chevrotain 10/km2 of its habitat [18],[19]; bay and Peters's duikers 2/km2 each (field 0.6-15.5 [21],[22]); red river hog 1/km2 (field 1-6 [26]); forest buffalo 0.2/km2 (Lopé 5/km2 locally [27], far lower forest-wide: assumption); sitatunga 0.2/km2 (swamps only: assumption); golden cat 6/100 km2 (field 3.8-16.2 [30]); leopard 4/100 km2 (field 2.7-12.1 [4],[7]), now that the mid-sized prey that feeds forest leopards is present

bay_duiker.body: [21]: 18-24 kg, shoulder 0.45-0.52 m; sexes alike (assumption: females slightly larger, as in most duikers)
bay_duiker.locomotion/senses/escape: assumption: as the blue duiker, scaled to a 20 kg duiker
bay_duiker.diet: [21]: frugivore (fruit and seed, modelled as 'roots') plus leaves; intake and water are assumptions
bay_duiker.lifecycle: [21]: gestation ~240 d, 1 young, female maturity ~18 months, up to 17 y in captivity (assumption: 12 y wild, ~300 d between births)

peters_duiker.body: [22]: 15-24 kg (mean 20.1; 16.5 in the Central African Republic), shoulder 0.45-0.60 m
peters_duiker.social: [22]: solitary, one male overlapping several females; female range ~0.4 km2
peters_duiker.lifecycle: [22]: gestation ~240 d, 1 young, maturity ~18 months (assumption: as the bay duiker otherwise)

red_river_hog.locomotion: assumption: from the island wild boar; good swimmer [24] but placed on land
red_river_hog.diet: [24],[26]: omnivore: roots, fruit, fungi, invertebrates, carrion (modelled as the boar's roots diet)
red_river_hog.social: [24],[26]: sounders of 6-20 with one boar; aggregations over 60
red_river_hog.lifecycle: [24],[25]: gestation 120-127 d, litter 1-6 (mean 3-4), one litter a year; maturity assumption 2 y; 15-20 y

forest_buffalo.locomotion: assumption: from the gaur, favouring bais and grassland
forest_buffalo.diet: [27]: grazer of bais and clearings, some browse
forest_buffalo.social: [27]: stable mixed herds averaging 12 (3-24); female range 4.6 km2 at Lopé
forest_buffalo.lifecycle: [25]: gestation ~340 d, 1 calf, maturity 3.5-5 y (assumption: 20 y, ~600 d between calves)
forest_buffalo.predation: [3],[27]: leopards take calves and young; adults are above the leopard's maxPreyKg

sitatunga.body: [28]: 40-120 kg, males about twice females; shoulder 0.75-1.25 m
sitatunga.locomotion: [28]: excellent swimmer, submerges to the nostrils (dive 120 s, assumption); land speeds assumption
sitatunga.diet: [28]: browse, reeds and grasses of marsh and swamp forest
sitatunga.social: [28]: solitary or small groups of females
sitatunga.lifecycle: [28]: gestation ~7-7.5 months, 1 young, maturity 1-2 y (female); up to 19 y (assumption: 12 y wild)

african_golden_cat.body: [29],[30]: ~5.5-16 kg, males larger (assumption: female 7, male 11); shoulder ~0.4 m
african_golden_cat.locomotion: [29]: climbs; speeds are assumptions for a 9 kg cat
african_golden_cat.diet/hunting: [30],[6]: mainly rodents, also small duikers and primates; the sim has no rodents, so blue duikers and the young of larger prey stand in (assumption); max prey 8 kg (assumption)
african_golden_cat.escape: [6]: highest trophic overlap with the leopard of any pair; avoids leopards
african_golden_cat.social: [29],[30]: solitary; 16.2 per 100 km2 unhunted, 3.8 where snared; territory sizes are assumptions from that density
african_golden_cat.lifecycle: assumption: gestation 75 d (as other Caracal), 1-2 kittens, mature 18 months, 12 y
african_golden_cat.diet/offRosterShare: assumption 0.6, informed by Hart, Katembo & Punga 1996 (Ituri, scats): rodents 50.9% and ungulates 20.2% of prey items, mean prey 1.4 kg; [30]: mainly rodents
